title: MacArthur returns to Leyte
body:
General Douglas MacArthur waded ashore at Red Beach on Leyte, keeping his promise to return to the Philippines.

On the beach he spoke into a radio microphone: "People of the Philippines, I have returned!"
photoNote: MacArthur and staff wading ashore. U.S. Army Signal Corps, Gaetano Faillace, NARA 531424, public domain.

video.note: PHILIPPINE OPERATIONS, Leyte Gulf, Oct 1944. U.S. Army Signal Corps film 111-ADC-3205 (NARA 17008), silent. MacArthur with Kenney, Sutherland, and Osmena in a landing craft headed for Red Beach, boats at the beach, then MacArthur and party walking inland on Leyte. U.S. government work, public domain. Clip uses 2:53.2 to 2:59.2, 3:08.5 to 3:13, and 3:19 to 3:26.

videoAlt.note: PHILIPPINE OPERATIONS, LEYTE, 20 Oct 1944. U.S. Army Signal Corps film 111-ADC-3075 (NARA 16878), silent. Troops of the 24th Infantry Division at Red Beach. U.S. government work, public domain. Clip uses 0:12 to 0:17, 0:21 to 0:25.5, and 4:24 to 4:31.

kit.filmCaption: Film from Leyte, 20 October 1944. General MacArthur rides a landing craft toward Red Beach with President Sergio Osmeña of the Philippines, then heads inland. U.S. Army Signal Corps footage.
